newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria, Italy in talks over cancelled LNG deal.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria, Italy in talks over cancelled LNG deal.

text.p: Nigeria and Italy have been into talks aimed at reaching an amicable out-of-court settlement over the cancellation of the gas purchase contract by Italian state power firm Enel, oil minister Dan Etete said.

"The federal government has been receiving encouraging response from the Italian government," Etete told said on Saturday in southeastern Bonny town, construction site of the $4 billion liquefied natural gas plant (LNG).
Work has been at full blast this year on the Nigerian LNG project which is to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of gas per year from 1999.
Arbitration between the two parties is underway after Enel in December pulled out of the contract to buy 3.5 billion cubic metres of gas per year.
Enel linked its decision to its abandonment for technical, economic and environmental reasons of its own project to construct a terminal to receive the gas.
Etete said: "The possibility of Enel receiving about 50 percent of the product they signed on with Nigeria LNG at a location where they have an infrastructure is being exploited.
"They will also find a way absolving the other fifty percent."
Last week, Theo Oerlemans, the Dutch chief executive of the NLNG, told Reuters the company was not looking for an alternative buyer for Enel's cancelled order.
"We are not trying to sell to anyone else, although there certainly has been interest," Oerlemans said.
Etete said the Enel issue would not affect the completion date of the project, adding that he was satisfied with the progress of construction work, which had reached a level of 30 percent completion.
Wim Kemper, the project's construction manager, said the project would be fifty percent complete by the end of this year.
Officials said the foundation laying ceremony of the project would be performed later this month.
Shell Gas BV is the technical leader with 25.6 percent of the equity in the NLNG joint venture with state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp which has 49 percent.
The other partners are Elf Aquitaine with 15 percent and Italy's Agip with 10.4 percent.
Long-term supply contracts has been signed with Enagas of Spain, Gaz de France and Botas of Turkey.
